Adaptive Traffic Steering automatically redirects application traffic to healthier network paths when network degradation affects connectivity or performance. This helps maintain application availability and minimize service disruptions caused by network congestion, packet loss, increased latency, and regional network outages.

You can enable Adaptive Traffic Steering for application segments in organizations that have Business Continuity configured. When enabled, Private Access (ZPA) uses real-time network health metrics to identify degraded paths and redirect traffic to alternative paths.
For more information, see Understanding Adaptive Traffic Steering⁠.
An update was released to support Adaptive Traffic Steering to help prioritize and redirect traffic for mission-critical applications at the Application segment level.
To learn more, see Adaptive Traffic Steering.

See image.
When enabled, users can access their configured browser extensions in the Zero Trust Mode menu while in an isolation session.

To learn more, see Using Browser Extensions in Isolation, Creating Isolation Profiles for Private Access, and Using the Zero Trust Mode Menu in Native Browser Experience.

blocks.heading: Global Rules and Policy Groups for Application Access

blocks.text: Private Access (ZPA) supports global rules and policy groups to simplify the management of application access policies.
Global rules let you define common rule logic once and apply it consistently across application access policies, reducing repetitive configuration and helping maintain consistent policy enforcement.
See image.
To learn more, see About Access Policies for Global Rules.

Policy groups provide a logical way to organize related application access policies by grouping rules that share common access requirements. Common criteria configured at the policy group level are automatically applied to every rule in the group and combined with each rule's criteria. This simplifies policy management, reduces repetitive configuration, and improves scalability as your deployment grows.
See image.
To learn more, see About Access Policies for Policy Groups.

blocks.heading: Notification Service Updates for VPN (for Legacy Apps)

blocks.text: The Notifications service supports Network Connector and VPN Service Edge notifications for the VPN (for Legacy Apps) category for the following Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) events:

blocks.item: Established peers count dropped: Indicates when the total number of active, established BGP sessions falls below a specified threshold.
Network routes count dropped: Indicates when there is a significant decrease in the number of network routes (prefixes) being received.
Peer disconnected: Indicates when a specific BGP session with a peer transitions to disconnected.
Peer extended downtime: Indicates when a BGP peer remains disconnected for a prolonged period.
Peer flapping: Indicates when a BGP peer's session repeatedly and rapidly cycles between up and down.

blocks.text: VPN Service Edge also supports notifications for the System Resource category for a CPU starvation event.
To learn more, see Support for VPN (for Legacy Apps) Notifications.

blocks.heading: Support for IdP Attribute-Based VPN Access Policy

blocks.text: Attribute objects distinguish between network-based IP address objects and identity provider (IdP) attribute objects. This allows you to create more powerful, identity-aware access policies by using SAML and SCIM attributes from your IdP directly in your rules.
See image.
To learn more, see About IP Address Objects and About IdP Attribute Objects.

blocks.heading: Actions for Upgrading Agent Groups in Microsegmentation

blocks.text: You can take the following actions when upgrading virtual machine (VM) agent groups for Microsegmentation in the Zscaler Admin Console:

blocks.item: Halt an upgrade that is in progress from the Upgrade Status column on the Agent Groups page.

Set the upgrade window when configuring an agent group. For example, if you start the upgrade at 8:00 AM and set the upgrade window to 12 hours, then the final agent upgrade required for the group starts no later than 8:00 PM.
Select the upgrade sequence (Serial or Parallel) and strategy (Halt next agent upgrade or Skip to next agent) when initiating an on-demand upgrade.

blocks.text: To learn more, see About Agent Groups, Configuring Agent Groups, and Managing Agent Groups.

blocks.heading: Perimeter Policies for Resource Groups in Microsegmentation

blocks.text: Perimeter policies allow you to systematically secure managed resource groups in Microsegmentation. You can create perimeter policies to easily define how Microsegmentation handles the resource group's inbound, outbound, and internal traffic (e.g., Block, Sim Block, Allow).
You can create a perimeter policy from the new Perimeter Policies page in the Zscaler Admin Console or from the Resource Groups page when creating a resource group.
See image.
To learn more, see About Perimeter Policies, Adding a Perimeter Policy, and Configuring Resource Groups.

blocks.heading: Policy Recommendations for Resource Groups in Microsegmentation

blocks.text: Microsegmentation provides policy recommendations for resource groups based on historical network flows. When selecting a resource group on the Application Map in the Zscaler Admin Console, you can view managed and unmanaged flows in a table. At the same time, a drawer opens with the option to review policy recommendations based on these flows.
See image.

Recommendations are listed on a page within the resource group. You can filter managed and unmanaged flows by direction (i.e., inbound and outbound). You can review and accept a recommendation as is, quickly applying the new policy and protecting flows. Alternatively, you can edit the recommendation, resolving conflicts as required, before applying it as a new policy or merging it with an existing policy for your organization.
See image.
To learn more, see Viewing the Application Map, About Policy Recommendations for Resource Groups, and Reviewing Policy Recommendations for Resource Groups.

blocks.heading: Enhancements for End User Isolation Experience for File Transfers

blocks.text: The following updates have been made to the end user isolation experience for Zero Trust Browser:

blocks.item: Download Completion: When a user downloads a file while in isolation, a temporary notification appears to confirm when the file has completed downloading. The user can click the View button from the notification to see the file name and location in the Protected Storage. Additionally, they can click the Protected Storage icon from the Zero Trust Mode menu to open the Protected Storage section and view all file transfer notifications.

Upload Options: A user can upload a file in multiple different ways while in isolation, such as using the Upload File button in the Protected Storage and uploading files from their local machine to a website.

blocks.text: To learn more, see Using the Zero Trust Mode Menu in Native Browser Experience and Transferring and Viewing Files in Isolation.

blocks.heading: Enhancements for End User Isolation Experience Session Indicator & Menu

blocks.text: The Zero Trust Mode icon that indicates a live isolation session for Zero Trust Browser hides an expandable menu for the user to access different functions:

blocks.item: The Protected Storage icon allows users to view all file transfers for the isolation session.
The Clipboard icon allows users to view notifications about clipboard functions and restrictions.
The Print icon allows users to view options and information for printing settings.
The Troubleshoot icon allows users to start a debug session, view network latency, access ip.zscaler.com, or export isolation session logs.
The Information icon allows users to view the settings configured by admins for an isolation profile. This includes user restrictions and disabled tools.

blocks.text: Clicking the checkmark Zero Trust Mode icon at the bottom of the menu collapses the options back under the floating icon.
See image.
To learn more, see Using the Zero Trust Mode Menu in Native Browser Experience.

blocks.heading: Agents Exclude Infrastructure Traffic from Flow Logs

blocks.text: Agents on the Windows operating system exclude infrastructure traffic (i.e., loopback IP addresses) from the flow logs, reducing noise and improving visibility. With this update, both Windows and Linux agents provide this streamlined flow data for organizations to monitor and analyze.
To learn more, see About Flow Logs.

Isolated sessions now automatically restore their web pages if they time out on a user's device. If a session is idle for longer than the timeout of 10 minutes, the isolated page automatically refreshes itself. When this action occurs, the banner notification announcing the start of isolation is disabled. This feature is different from Persistent State, which is enabled per isolation profile to carry over data from an expired session to a new session.

blocks.heading: OAuth 2.0 Enrollment Support for Private Cloud Controllers

blocks.text: An update was released to support OAuth 2.0 enrollment for Private Cloud Controllers. OAuth 2.0 is the recommended method for enrollment for Private Access (ZPA), but provisioning key enrollment is also supported. To use OAuth 2.0, the OAuth server FQDN zpa-oauth.private.zscaler.com must be allowlisted, and user devices must be allowed to make an outbound connection to the zpa-oauth.private.zscaler.com server. Refer to config.zscaler.com/private.zscaler.com/zpa (for the private.zscaler.com cloud) or config.zscaler.com/zpatwo.net/zpa (for the zpatwo.net cloud) for the IP address to add to the allowlist.
OAuth 2.0 support is available with a minimum version of Manager software and Private Cloud Controller version 25.47.3.

Supported virtual machine (VM) images automatically have this feature enabled. Provisioning key enrollment is also supported on all VM images. The image attempts to use OAuth enrollment tokens by default but applies a provisioning key first if one is available.
The OAuth server only supports IPv4-based communication. If a Private Cloud Controller only has an IPV6 address, it cannot access the OAuth server.
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring Private Cloud Controllers.

blocks.text: An update was released to provide support for end user migration to Authentication Service. This update ensures that the set of existing Private Access (ZPA) end users and their entitlements remain accurate and consistent throughout the migration process. Several new statuses are available for filtering Agent Telemetry results.
For agents, the following statuses are available:

blocks.item: Up to Date: The new agent upgrade version number is either greater than or equal to the agent version number of its corresponding agent group.
Pending: The new agent upgrade version number is less than the agent version number of its corresponding agent group.
In Progress: The agent is actively upgrading, and will complete within 10 minutes of reaching this status.
Forced Upgrade: The agent has manually been upgraded by an admin outside its configured upgrade schedule.
Failed: An upgrade attempt has failed.
N/A: The agent or its agent group is disabled.

blocks.text: For agent groups, the following statuses are available:

blocks.item: Up to Date: All agents are up-to-date.
Pending: At least one agent in the agent group is in a pending status for the latest agent version.
In Progress: At least one agent in the agent group is actively upgrading.
In Progress with Failures: Multiple agents in an agent group are upgrading with some in a failed state and the remaining agents proceeding.
Failed: All agents within an agent group have reached a failed state.
Completed with Failures: All agents within an agent group have completed the upgrade process with some in a failed state.
N/A: The agent group is disabled.

blocks.text: To learn more, see About Agent Telemetry.

blocks.heading: Tag Management for Defined Application Segments

blocks.text: Private Access (ZPA) supports Tag Management, which enables you to create, organize, and manage tags for classifying and grouping resources more effectively. Tag Management standardizes tagging across environments to simplify policy configuration and improve visibility into related resources within Private Access. To learn more, see About Tag Management for Application Segments.
See image.

With Tag Management, you can configure namespaces to logically organize tags and avoid naming conflicts, as well as add and configure tags within those namespaces. When configuring namespaces, you can assign optional values to tags to enable discovery and logical grouping, and configure tag groups by grouping related tags using shared values. To learn more, see Configuring Tags and Namespaces for Application Segments.
See image.
Namespaces and tags can be assigned to defined application segments. To learn more, see Configuring Defined Application Segments.
See image.
Tag groups and tag values can be assigned to access policies. To learn more, see Configuring Access Policy.
See image.
The maximum number of tags that can be created per Microtenant is 25,000. The maximum number of tags that can be created per customer is 25,000. To learn more, see Ranges & Limitations.

blocks.heading: Replacing or Migrating Existing Network Connectors with Network Connectors that Support Redundancy

blocks.text: For customers who are not yet running Network Connectors that support redundancy, Zscaler strongly recommends replacing or migrating existing Network Connectors with redundancy-capable Network Connectors. Network Connectors that support redundancy resolve the following failure scenarios:

blocks.item: An internal link failure towards customer routers
An external link failure towards the VPN Service Edge
A complete Network Connector node failure
A data center failure with traffic rerouting towards another data center
Scaling - ECMP (equal-cost multi-path) load balancing across Network Connectors from the VPN Service Edges and customer routers towards the Network Connector

blocks.text: The redundancy design is based on External Border Gateway Protocol (EBGP) routing.
To learn more, see High Availability and Redundancy in VPN (for Legacy Apps) and Replacing or Migrating Existing Network Connectors with Network Connectors that Support Redundancy.

blocks.heading: Access Policies for VPN (for Legacy Apps)

blocks.text: VPN (for Legacy Apps) provides access policy rules that can allow or block network traffic on VPN Service Edges. To create a rule, you need to define the source and destination IP addresses as well as the protocol used. An address book consists of Classless Inter-Domain Routing (CIDRs) and IP addresses that can be used as a source or destination network in multiple policy rules to help organize the network resources to protect.

Per ZPA policy evaluation, VPN (for Legacy Apps) evaluates access policy rules using a top-down, specific-match principle. Traffic that doesn't match any access policy rule is blocked by default. If you are new to VPN (for Legacy Apps), you must create a policy rule to allow any traffic through the VPN tunnel.
VPN (for Legacy Apps) supports a maximum of 1,000 policy rules and 128 address book entries.
This release includes the following enhancements for access policies:

blocks.item: You can view configured rules and their actions on the Rules page. You can also:
View how many additional source or destination networks are available. By default, two networks display but if there are more, the number of additional networks appears (e.g., +1).
Select a value in the Rule Order column to change the order in which rules are evaluated. Rules are evaluated using a top-down, first-match principle.
Select a rule name to view details for the rule.

When adding a rule for the source or destination network, you can manually enter it, import individual LAN/Client Subnet entries, or select entries from the address book. You can expand the list of added entries under the IP Address field.

If you manually enter or import LAN/Client Subnet entries, each time you update a Network segment, you must make a corresponding change to the access policy to add the LAN/Client Subnet entries. If you use the address book, any host or subnet added to the address book is automatically added to the access policy.
On the Address Book page, you can view, search, add, edit, or delete defined sets of IP addresses and CIDRs.

You can add a set of IP addresses or CIDRs to the address book. A set of addresses in the address book cannot be nested inside of other address books, but you can reuse IP addresses and CIDRs in different address books.

blocks.text: You can now configure a timer for the automatic age-out of disconnected agents for individual agent groups. When the timer is enabled, you can set the duration of days, hours, or minutes before access expires.

Microsegmentation now provides visibility to resources such as deployments, statefulsets, replicasets, and daemonsets. When you deploy agents, you can view network flows in the Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) Admin Portal.

You can now use tags to annotate resources with metadata that can be used when defining membership criteria for resource groups. You can create namespaces, tag keys, and tag groups and assign them to managed resources. To learn more, see Configuring Resource Groups.

blocks.heading: Automated Manager Software Updates for Private Service Edges and Private Cloud Controller

blocks.text: An update was released to support automated updates to the Manager software and software updates for ZPA Private Service Edge and Private Cloud Controller.
Automated Manager software updates are available with a Manager software version of 25.46.3 or later and a ZPA Private Service Edge or Private Cloud Controller version of 25.46.3 or later.
The table includes the following updates:

blocks.item: Version Profile: Displays the version profile applied to the ZPA Private Service Edge or Private Cloud Controller. You can hover over the information icon under the Version Profile column heading to view the target version for the Manager software and ZPA Private Service Edge or Private Cloud Controller software.

Software Update: Displays the status of the ZPA Private Service Edge or Private Cloud Controller software update. You can hover over the information icon next to the update status to view more information, such as the scheduled version and upgrade window.

Manager Update: Displays the status of the Manager software update. You can hover over the information icon next to the update status to view more information, such as the scheduled version and upgrade window.
When viewing details for a ZPA Private Service Edge or Private Cloud Controller, you can view the Last Manager Update time.

blocks.text: To learn more, see About ZPA Private Service Edges or About Private Cloud Controllers.
Manager software updates are scheduled during the maintenance window for ZPA software updates.

This release fixes an intermittent issue with VPN redundancy where upgrading the VPN Service Edge caused it to lose the Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) override configuration file upon restart, which resulted in the BGP neighborship between the Network Connector and VPN Service Edge dropping until the configuration file was manually reuploaded.
To learn more, see About VPN Service Edges.

A new client type and criteria for Extranet is supported when configuring an access policy. The Extranet client type and criteria allow admins to assign an extranet to an application segment to provide a defined set of partners, and supports both location and sublocation for extranet traffic. The same functionality is supported via the cloud service API.
See image.
To learn more, see About Extranet, About Access Policy, and Configuring Access Policies.
An update was released to support adding more metadata for tagging applications to provide a more granular grouping and access management strategy.
To learn more, see Tag Management for Defined Application Segments.

blocks.heading: Using the Application Map for Microsegmentation

blocks.text: The Application Map for Microsegmentation is a visual representation of your network data and how it all works together. The interactive graph provides widgets for resource group, Public Internet, and VPC/VNET data that can aid in policy configuration and general resource maintenance.
See image.
To learn more, see Viewing the Application Map.
